Understanding the Portfolio Structure

Sophisticated portfolios demand a balance between public equity alpha and private market growth. This analysis outlines key variables across both asset classes:

  • 01 · Scale Assets Under Management (AUM) Varies from boutique to massive institutional scale (₹14,222 Cr).
  • 02 · Performance Multi-Horizon Track Record Analyzing 6-month, 1-year, 2-year, and 3/5-year CAGR returns to ensure consistent alpha generation.
  • 03 · Liquidity Liquidity & Fees PMS offers daily liquidity with flat management fees. AIF involves longer lock-ins with performance fees structured above hurdle rates.

Portfolio Takeaways  ·  Data as on 30th June 2026

Key Strategic Insights

Finding 01

High Alpha Specialists Lead Public Returns

Stallion Asset's Core Fund and Green Lantern Capital's Growth Fund demonstrate extraordinary performance with 3-year CAGRs of 36.27% and 35.25% respectively. Both are correctly pre-curated on our preferred shortlist, capturing maximum public-equity alpha.

Shortlist focuses on pure alpha
Finding 02

AIF Structure Yields Private Market Premiums

AIFs analyzed target high-conviction growth pipelines with 26-32% IRR projections, seeking startups and pre-IPO entities (e.g. Smallcase, Shadowfax, Giva). These assets are unavailable via traditional public equity markets.

Private opportunities unlock upside
Finding 03

Structured Hurdle Guardrails Mitigate Risk

Category II AIFs represent longer lock-ins (5-7Y). EAAA addresses liquidity constraints by supporting Loan Against Securities (LAS), while Oister Ace III and Nippon Nidi 2A focus on strict cash flow. High hurdles (10-12.5%) ensure managers only gain performance carry when exceeding base market expectations.

Hurdles protect investor capital
Vehicle Structure Comparison  ·  Data as on 30th June 2026

PMS vs. AIF Structural Trade-Offs

A breakdown of the legal, regulatory, and mechanical differences that dictate product fit for individual HNW client situations.

Dimension Portfolio Management Services (PMS) Alternative Investment Funds (AIF)
Regulatory Minimum ₹50 Lakhs ₹1 Crore
Portfolio Ownership Discretionary or Non-Discretionary individual client demat holdings. Assets belong directly to the client. Pooled trust structure (Category II AIF). Client owns units representing proportional share of the fund assets.
Taxation Mode Passed through directly. Client pays Short-Term (STCG) and Long-Term Capital Gains (LTCG) on every transaction. Taxed at the fund level. Net distributions are typically tax-free or pre-taxed based on trust structure.
Liquidity & Exit High liquidity. Exit possible on any business day, subject to sliding exit loads (e.g. 1-3% in year 1). Locked structure (typically 5-7 years). EAAA permits Loan Against Securities (LAS) to mitigate lock-ins; Nippon and Oister do not support LAS.
Fee Architecture Typically flat management fee (1.5 - 2.5% p.a.) or hybrid sharing models. Rarely incorporates performance hurdle guards. Base management fee (1.65 - 2.00%) + Performance fee (16.5 - 20.0% carry) strictly over hurdle rates (10 - 12.5%).
Investment Mandate Exclusively listed public securities (equities and liquid debt instruments). Unlisted growth companies, private venture debt, startups, and late-stage pre-IPO equities.
